intended_object: The Künneth isomorphism ⨁_{p+q=n} H_p(X; M) ⊗ H_q(Y; N) ≅ H_n(X × Y; M ⊗ N) for singular homology, induced by the homology cross product. It holds when the singular chain complexes split: cycles split off the chains and homology splits off the cycles, as happens for example over a field. This is inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is `asIso` applied to `singularHomologyKunneth X Y M N n`.

**The map.** `singularHomologyKunneth` is the algebraic Künneth map of the singular chain complexes, followed by the map on homology induced by the shuffle (Eilenberg–Zilber) map. Lemma `ι_singularHomologyKunneth` shows that on each summand it restricts to the homology cross product. So the source, the degree-n part of the tensor product of graded objects ⨁_{p+q=n} H_p(X; M) ⊗ H_q(Y; N), and the target, H_n(X × Y; M ⊗ N), are the right ones. The map is the standard Künneth map.

**Why it is an isomorphism.** The `IsIso` instance comes from the hypotheses that cycles are split subobjects of the chains and homology is a split quotient of the cycles. Under these hypotheses the Tor term in the Künneth short exact sequence vanishes and the algebraic Künneth map is an isomorphism. The shuffle map is a chain homotopy equivalence, so the topological map is one as well.

**Generality.** The hypotheses are a standard sufficient condition. They hold for all modules over a field, or more generally for semisimple coefficients. So the definition is at least as general as the textbook statement over a field. The setting is modules over an arbitrary commutative ring with splitting assumptions, which is natural. An isomorphism can only be constructed under hypotheses that make the map invertible, so this is not an artificial narrowing. The general Künneth map itself is defined elsewhere in the file for a general preadditive monoidal category C.
